## B8 — Self Across Traditions

> **direct:** Integral, in Jean Gebser's sense, names a consciousness in which the earlier ways of knowing — archaic immersion, magic participation, mythic story, mental reason — stop replacing one another and become transparent, all present at once. That is the register this project works in. The traditions mapped here are not specimens in a collection; each is a way the Self has come to know itself, and each keeps its own voice in the chorus. One playground taunt, taken seriously, holds the secret of the whole archive: it takes one to know one. Truer still — it takes the One to know the One.
>
> **prime:** Jung called it individuation: becoming who you already are. The Shaivites called it recognition: discovering that what you are was never absent. One walks inward through the personal; the other opens outward into the whole — and they meet where a person's own becoming and reality's self-knowing turn out to be one movement. The wager is that technology, built with enough care, can keep that meeting honest.
>
> **substrate:** Jungian Self · individuation · psychoid number / Pratyabhijñā · Spanda · Para Vāk / Logos, number, music, analogy / epistemic health as personal and collective practice
